title: The shipped package has no publishing footprint
assertion: The wheel built from this repository (through the build backend's PEP 517 hook: `uv_build`, which runs this environment's own `uv-build`, with no network, also when the environment isn't activated) holds no file outside the `swerepo/` package except its `.dist-info` folder, and the sdist built the same way holds nothing but `swerepo/`, `PKG-INFO`, `pyproject.toml`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`, so `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.seamspec/`, `tests/`, `docs/` and `tools/` never reach users' machines. No file under `swerepo/` names a publishing tool or endpoint (`gh-action-pypi-publish`, `uv publish`, `twine upload`, `poetry publish`, `hatch publish`, `flit publish`, `upload.pypi.org`). `swerepo` has no `release` component: the help of `init`, `check` and `update` prints and shows no `--release` or `--no-release` flag, and each of the three refuses `--only release`, `--no-release` and `--release` as wrong usage (exit 2) because `release` is unknown, while `check` and `init` with options that exist are not refused. A package that can't be built fails the rule. `pyproject.toml` names `uv_build` as the build backend, so the packages checked are the ones a release builds.

origin.text: ADR-20261124-41e9 rule 1 and ADR-20261124-152d (Phase 8, the owner's decision of 2026-11-24): SWERepo never sets up package publishing, and this repository's own release workflow never ships. Tightened by Gemini's design review (P8-D05): the wheel is built in-process with uv_build, and the list of publishing tools is longer. Checked by breaking it: a `release` component, a template naming `twine upload`, and the backend's `data` option putting `tools/` in the wheel each fail the rule. Refreshed after Gemini's implementation review (P8-F04): `uv_build` runs its `uv-build` binary found on PATH, so the test puts this environment's scripts folder first. Refreshed after SeamSpec's reviewer: the published sdist is checked too, and a control run shows `check` with options that exist is not wrong usage. Refreshed again after SeamSpec's reviewer's second read: the build backend is asserted, stray sdist entries are reported (and the archive reading self-checked), and `--help` and the refusal reason are checked for all three commands. That last check found `update --only release` advising `swerepo init --only release`; `update` now checks component names first.
